# SQL Server Integration Services

Microsoft's ETL tool: packages authored as `.dtsx` in Visual Studio / SSDT, built from a **control
flow** of tasks and, inside a Data Flow Task, a **data flow** of typed sources, transforms and
destinations. [[data-warehousing-and-business-intelligence]] ships two packages, and they use the
tool in two different ways.

## Package 1 — control flow only

`etl/ssis/Package.dtsx` builds a `list_four` schema entirely out of Execute SQL tasks. SSIS is doing
orchestration here, not transformation: the SQL is the deliverable and the package is the runner.
Two things about it are worth recording.

- Its `DIM_CUSTOMER` load joins addresses through the store id only, where the hand-written
  `sql/02_star_schema/` version uses a coalesce across store and person and says why.
- It creates a `load_status` table and populates it with `'Success'` string literals — a row per
  table, written unconditionally. The hand-written load replaces exactly this with row counts and
  anti-join integrity checks, and argues the case in a comment. That contrast is the whole of
  [[verify-the-load-dont-declare-it]], and it is unusual to have both the pattern and its
  counter-example in one repository.

The two schemas disagree on column set and defaults and were never reconciled — one of four recorded
instances of [[documentation-drift]] in this repo, and an example of
[[keep-the-superseded-version-in-tree]].

## Package 2 — a real data flow

`project/twtr/ssis/Package.dtsx` is the conventional shape: a Flat File source and an OLE DB
destination inside one Data Flow Task, landing a CSV of daily price bars into a `staging.quotes`
table. The staging table carries two `CHECK` constraints at the door — a high/low ordering rule and
a non-negative volume rule — so malformed rows fail at the boundary rather than propagating into the
star. Loading order from there on is [[etl-load-order]]; the destination model is [[star-schema]].

The CSV itself is git-ignored, so the package is committed without the input it consumes.

## Working with `.dtsx` in version control

A package is XML, so it diffs — in principle. In practice a 23 KB and a 37 KB file of generated
markup with embedded, newline-escaped SQL is not reviewable by reading the diff, and the SQL inside
it is invisible to any tool that greps `*.sql`. That is a real argument for the shape this repo
mostly settled on: keep the logic in `.sql` files, and let the package be a thin runner over them.

## Status

Both packages are Visual Studio project sources, not deployed to any SSIS catalog. `docs/star-schema.md`
makes the same disclosure for the [[ssas]] side. Nothing here executes on a clean clone — it needs
SSDT and a live [[sql-server]] instance.
